content.value_statement: MSBuild and package version rules can drift across large .NET repositories. This skill runs a focused linter and explains violations.
actual_capabilities: Runs the configured .NET architecture linter against the current repository.
Reports rule identifiers, file paths, line numbers, and violation details.
Checks hardcoded package versions in Central Package Management files.
Flags Version.props imports outside the documented allowed owners.
Explains the clean output message when all lint rules pass.
limitations: Requires the referenced lint-dotnet.sh script to exist and be executable.
Only checks rules implemented by the external linter script.
Does not build, test, or restore the .NET project.
Best fits repositories using the documented MSBuild and CPM layout.

use_cases.title: Check package governance before review
use_cases.description: Run the linter before a pull request to catch hardcoded package versions and invalid imports.

use_cases.title: Maintain shared MSBuild conventions
use_cases.description: Verify that repository files follow the allowed Version.props ownership model.

use_cases.title: Audit migration cleanup work
use_cases.description: Find remaining CPM and MSBuild rule violations during package management migrations.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic lint check
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the lint-dotnet skill on this repository and summarize any violations in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Review package version rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use lint-dotnet to check CPM package version rules. Group results by rule and suggest the smallest safe fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a migration cleanup plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Run lint-dotnet, explain which files import Version.props incorrectly, and produce a prioritized cleanup plan for the team.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a pull request for architecture drift
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before merging shared build changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Run lint-dotnet against the current checkout, compare findings with the intended MSBuild architecture, and recommend reviewer actions.

output_examples.input: Ask the skill to check a repository with hardcoded package versions.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the rule, affected files, line numbers, and a fix using a shared version variable.

output_examples.input: Ask the skill to verify a repository with no lint violations.
output_examples.output: The response reports that all rules passed and says the repository is ready for the next validation step.

output_examples.input: Ask the skill to review incorrect Version.props imports.
output_examples.output: The response lists the invalid import owners and explains which documented files may own the import.

best_practices: Confirm shell command execution before running the skill in any repository.
Run the linter in a clean working tree before changing shared build files.
Review lint output with repository owners before applying architecture changes.
anti_patterns: Do not run the skill on an untrusted repository without command approval.
Do not treat passing lint as proof that builds or tests pass.
Do not copy Version.props when the repository requires a symlink.

faq.question: What does this skill check?
faq.answer: It checks documented .NET architecture rules for MSBuild files, CPM package versions, and Version.props imports.

faq.question: Does it modify files automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill description runs a linter and reports violations. Fixes should be requested and reviewed separately.

faq.question: Does it need shell access?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs the agent to run a bash script from CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What happens when no violations exist?
faq.answer: The linter reports that all rules passed, then the workflow can continue to other validation steps.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for builds or tests?
faq.answer: No. Use it with normal .NET restore, build, and test workflows.
